answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when an independent audit proves fraud. Splitting one attacker across a grove of fresh accounts does not multiply influence for free: every account must tie up capital, and coordinated accounts can lose it all if their outputs fail checks. Raising the stake toward its zenith makes mass impersonation costly, while pigment in a test fixture can mark outputs for audit without granting trusted status.
